status: docs-scoped structured proof; not production runtime authority

principles.atomicTruth: exact profile id + version + executable pattern id
principles.whyDefault: why the hand/event qualifies or is special; player strategy only when separately evidenced
principles.scoreAuthority: derive from exact treatment reference; do not treat learner prose as score authority

facetDefinitions.ordinary-grouped: Qualifying structure uses the ordinary four-melds-plus-pair decomposition.
facetDefinitions.irregular-hand: Qualifying structure does not use the ordinary four-melds-plus-pair decomposition.
facetDefinitions.event-defined: The winning event/context is essential to qualification.
facetDefinitions.one-suit: Qualifying suited tiles come from one numbered suit; honours may still be permitted or required.
facetDefinitions.multiple-suits: The qualifying structure explicitly uses more than one numbered suit.
facetDefinitions.pairs: Pairs are an essential structural feature.
facetDefinitions.pungs-kongs: Pungs and/or Kongs are essential structural features.
facetDefinitions.chow-involving: A Chow is required or explicitly permitted by the reviewed variant.
facetDefinitions.honours: Wind and/or Dragon tiles are structurally required.
facetDefinitions.knitted-interleave: Same-number tiles across suits form the defining interleaved structure.
facetDefinitions.green-tiles: Composition is restricted to Green Dragon and the permitted green Bamboo tiles.

entries.summary: Every suited 1 and 9, every Wind and Dragon, plus one duplicate.
entries.whatItIs: A 14-tile special hand containing one of each of the thirteen terminal and honour tile types, with one of those thirteen tiles duplicated.
entries.whatItMeans: Instead of building four normal melds and a pair, you complete a fixed collection of thirteen different terminal/honour tiles and then pair one of them.
entries.whySpecial: It qualifies through a complete non-standard collection rather than the ordinary four-melds-plus-pair structure.
howItWorks: Keep the 1 and 9 of all three suits.
Keep all four Winds and all three Dragons.
Complete one of each of those thirteen tile types.
Use the fourteenth tile to duplicate one of them.

treatmentTeaching.difference: Shared tile structure; exact BMJA score is derived from the treatment.
Same reviewed tile structure; Thompson & Maloney assigns a different fixed value.
Same reviewed tile structure; the current Outside the Box treatment additionally requires concealment.
Buzzard local name Thirteen Odd Majors; exact structural membership is source/runtime verified and its configured-limit score remains treatment-local.

watchOutFor: Do not try to split the hand into ordinary Chows and Pungs.
The duplicate may be any one of the thirteen required tile types in the reviewed shared concept.

entries.summary: Pungs or Kongs of all four Winds, plus a pair.
entries.whatItIs: A normal grouped Mahjong hand in which all four melds are Wind Pungs or Kongs, with one pair completing the hand.
entries.whatItMeans: All four Wind families are represented as complete triplet/quad sets rather than merely appearing somewhere in the hand.
entries.whySpecial: The entire four-meld structure is occupied by the four Winds, making the hand structurally distinctive while still using an ordinary grouped hand shape.
howItWorks: Make a Pung or Kong of East Wind.
Do the same for South, West and North.
Complete the hand with a pair.

treatmentTeaching.difference: Shared structure; BMJA score and intrinsic fishing-floor behaviour remain treatment-local.
Shared structure; Thompson & Maloney assigns its own fixed value.
Shared structure; Outside the Box retains its own exposure treatment.

entries.summary: A green-tile special built from Green Dragon and the green Bamboo tiles; the exact allowed meld structure differs by rules.
entries.whatItIs: A family of special-hand treatments restricted to Green Dragon and Bamboo 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8.
entries.whatItMeans: The shared idea is the restricted green tile set. British/BMJA and Outside the Box use a no-Chow Pung/Kong form; Thompson & Maloney permits one specific 2-3-4 Bamboo Chow.
entries.whySpecial: Almost the whole hand is constrained by tile identity and colour family, so a small rules difference about whether a Chow is allowed materially changes which hands qualify.

variants.label: British / Outside the Box form
variants.definition: Four Pung/Kong groups and a pair, all drawn from Green Dragon and Bamboo 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8; no Chow in the reviewed structure.

variants.label: Thompson & Maloney Western form
variants.definition: Uses the same green tile family but may contain one 2-3-4 Bamboo Chow.

entries.summary: One suit from 1 through 9 plus all four Winds and one duplicate; the narrower version fixes the duplicate as the suited 1.
entries.whatItIs: A reviewed family of irregular Snake hands built from a complete 1-9 run in one suit and all four Winds.
entries.whatItMeans: The two reviewed variants share the same thirteen-tile base. The narrower Wriggling Snake pairs the suited 1; the broader Wriggly Snake allows any tile in the base to be duplicated.
entries.whySpecial: The entire hand is a fixed loose-tile pattern rather than normal melds, and one apparently small pairing difference changes the valid set of hands.

variants.label: Wriggling Snake
variants.definition: 1-9 in one suit, all four Winds, with the suited 1 duplicated.

variants.label: Wriggly Snake
variants.definition: 1-9 in one suit, all four Winds, with any one tile in that thirteen-tile base duplicated.

entries.summary: Several special hands use seven pairs, but similar names do not mean the same qualification.
entries.whatItIs: A browse family connecting reviewed pair-based special hands while keeping their distinct predicates and names.
entries.whatItMeans: All Pair Honours, All Pair, Heavenly Twins and Seven Twins are useful to compare because all are pair-based, but they impose different tile and winning-method conditions.
entries.whySpecial: Seven-pair structures depart from the ordinary four-melds-plus-pair shape, and each named treatment adds its own restrictions.

variants.label: All Pair Honours
variants.definition: Seven pairs, each made from a Wind, Dragon, or suited 1/9.

variants.label: All Pair
variants.relation: name-collision with All Pair Honours; neither predicate contains the other
variants.definition: Seven pairs using at most one numbered suit, with honours allowed.

variants.label: Heavenly Twins
variants.definition: Seven pairs entirely in one numbered suit, without honours.

variants.label: Seven Twins
variants.relation: distinct effective qualification because the winning method matters
variants.definition: Seven distinct loose pairs plus the treatment's wall-based winning-method requirement.

entries.summary: An East player's already complete initial deal, named Heaven's Blessing in BMJA and Original Hand in Buzzard.
entries.whatItIs: A reviewed event family for a winning hand already complete in East’s original deal.
entries.whatItMeans: The shared current event predicate is East, initial deal, and a complete winning hand; Buzzard’s local names and source-verified provenance remain distinct from BMJA’s inferred source mapping.
entries.whySpecial: Mahjong is complete before ordinary play has begun.
howItWorks: The hand is already a legal Mahjong.
The win is recorded as the original-deal event.
entries.referenceNote: Buzzard source verifies East, original deal and already-complete hand. BMJA’s mapping remains inferred from “Mah Jong in original deal”; shared current predicate does not make the historical names universally equivalent.

entries.summary: A two-Kong replacement-tile sequence in which the second replacement completes Mahjong.
entries.whatItIs: A BMJA event-defined special based on two consecutive Kong/replacement events ending in Mahjong.
entries.whatItMeans: The final tiles alone are not enough; the order of Kong declarations and replacement draws is part of what qualifies the special.
entries.whySpecial: Qualification depends on an exact chain of events rather than only the completed hand shape.
howItWorks: Its replacement tile completes a second Kong.
The next replacement tile completes Mahjong.

entries.summary: A reviewed family of Dragon-set specials with distinct BMJA/T&M, Club - Bramhall 2026, and Buzzard winner predicates.
entries.whatItIs: A family connecting four exact profile treatments that require Pung or Kong sets of all three Dragons but differ in their remaining-set qualifications.
entries.whatItMeans: BMJA and T&M require a fourth Pung/Kong; Club - Bramhall 2026 allows a Chow, Pung or Kong when its fourth set and pair share one numbered suit; Buzzard allows any otherwise lawful ordinary fourth set and pair. These are related variants, not equivalent treatments.
entries.whySpecial: All variants centre on all three Dragon sets while their exact profile predicates remain distinct.

variants.label: Three Great Scholars — BMJA / Thompson & Maloney
variants.definition: All three Dragon Pung/Kongs plus a fourth Pung/Kong and a pair.

variants.label: Three Great Scholars — Club - Bramhall 2026
variants.definition: All three Dragon Pung/Kongs; the fourth meld may be a Chow, Pung or Kong, and it and the pair use the same numbered suit.

variants.label: Three Dragons — Buzzard 2000
variants.definition: All three Dragon Pung/Kongs plus any otherwise lawful ordinary fourth set and pair.

entries.referenceNote: The Buzzard incomplete Three-Dragon consequence is a structured profile-score-result link, not a special-hand detector or treatment ID.

entries.summary: Seven same-number pairs across exactly two suits; duplicate pairs are allowed where physical tile copies permit them.
entries.whatItIs: A pair-based irregular hand built by matching the same numbers across two different suits rather than making normal melds.
entries.whatItMeans: The hand has seven cross-suit same-number pairs and uses exactly two numbered suits throughout.
entries.whySpecial: The hand replaces the ordinary meld structure with a complete two-suit pairing pattern.

variants.label: Two-suit Knitting
variants.definition: Seven same-number cross-suit pairs across exactly two numbered suits; exact score and exposure rules remain attached to each profile treatment.

entries.summary: Four same-number groups across all three suits, plus a same-number pair across two suits.
entries.whatItIs: An irregular knitted hand built from four three-suit same-number groups and one cross-suit pair.
entries.whatItMeans: Each three-tile unit uses the same number once in each suit, and the final pair uses the same number in two suits.
entries.whySpecial: The whole hand follows a three-suit interleaving pattern rather than ordinary melds.

variants.label: Triple Knitting
variants.definition: Four three-suit same-number groups plus one same-number pair across two suits in a complete 14-tile loose layout; exact score and exposure rules remain attached to each profile treatment.

entries.displayName: Gates of Heaven / Calling Nine Tile Hand
entries.summary: A one-suit 1112345678999-style family whose permitted completion differs materially by rules.
entries.whatItIs: A reviewed family of one-suit irregular hands built around three 1s, three 9s and one each of 2 through 8, with rules-specific completion requirements.
entries.whatItMeans: The tile skeleton is closely related across profiles, but BMJA, Thompson & Maloney and Buzzard do not use identical completion/provenance semantics.
entries.whySpecial: A tightly constrained one-suit tile skeleton leaves only a small set of possible completions, so the exact allowed winning tile matters.

variants.label: BMJA Gates of Heaven
variants.definition: Uses the middle-rank duplicate skeleton and BMJA-specific completion/provenance logic.

variants.label: Western Gates of Heaven
variants.definition: Uses the one-suit 1112345678999 skeleton with a duplicated 2-8 tile; the treatment is concealed-only.

variants.label: Calling Nine Tile Hand
variants.definition: Starts from the 1112345678999 base and permits any same-suit 1-9 tile as the completing extra tile.
